f3_program: observe(at("employee.pay.regular_hourly_rate", "workweek"), 30, "dollar_per_hour", source("makes 30 dollars an hour for the first 40 hours in the workweek"))
observe(at("employee.pay.regular_hours_limit", "workweek"), 40, "hour", source("the first 40 hours in the workweek"))
observe(at("employee.pay.overtime_start_after_hours", "workweek"), 40, "hour", source("every hour above 40 in the week"))
percent_more(at("employee.pay.overtime_hourly_rate", "workweek"), at("employee.pay.regular_hourly_rate", "workweek"), 50, source("an additional 50% for every hour above 40 in the week"))
observe(at("employee.work.period.duration", "first_3_days"), 3, "day", source("first 3 days in the workweek"))
observe(at("employee.work.hours_per_day", "first_3_days"), 6, "hour_per_day", source("works 6 hours for the first 3 days in the workweek"))
observe(at("employee.work.period.duration", "remaining_2_days"), 2, "day", source("remaining 2 days"))
multiple(at("employee.work.hours_per_day", "remaining_2_days"), at("employee.work.hours_per_day", "first_3_days"), 2, source("twice as many hours per day for the remaining 2 days"))
query("value", at("employee.earnings.total", "workweek"))

assumptions: The requested earnings require equating each caught shrimp with one sale-counted shrimp tail, but that one-to-one ontology relation is not stated in the source or provided by F3-v1.

f3_program: collection("jeff.kitchen.cabinets", "cabinet", "jeff.kitchen", source("cabinets in his kitchen"))
observe(at("jeff.kitchen.cabinets.count", "initial"), 3, "count", source("He currently has 3 cabinets over one counter and no other cabinets"))
observe(at("jeff.kitchen.cabinets_per_counter", "initial"), 3, "count", source("3 cabinets over one counter"))
observe(at("jeff.kitchen.cabinet_counters.count", "initial"), 1, "count", source("one counter"))
observe(at("jeff.kitchen.new_cabinet_counters.count", "first_installation"), 3, "count", source("over 3 different counters each"))
multiple(at("jeff.kitchen.cabinets_per_counter", "first_installation"), at("jeff.kitchen.cabinets_per_counter", "initial"), 2, source("twice as many cabinets over 3 different counters each"))

product_relation("jeff.kitchen.first_installation.cabinets.count", at("jeff.kitchen.cabinets_per_counter", "first_installation"), at("jeff.kitchen.new_cabinet_counters.count", "first_installation"), source("He installs twice as many cabinets over 3 different counters each"))

add("install_over_counters", "jeff", at("jeff.kitchen.cabinets.count", "current"), "jeff.kitchen.first_installation.cabinets.count", source("He installs twice as many cabinets over 3 different counters each"))
add("install_five_more", "jeff", at("jeff.kitchen.cabinets.count", "current"), 5, source("He then installs 5 more cabinets"))
query("value", at("jeff.kitchen.cabinets.count", "current"))
assumptions: The phrase "twice as many cabinets over 3 different counters each" is interpreted as twice the existing per-counter cabinet count at each of the three new counters.
